newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down after rate cut.

text.p: * Central Bank sells $23 million to stop peso fall
The cut in the Central Bank's overnight rates on Monday pulled down the Philippine peso which settled last at 26.235 pesos to the dollar from the previous 26.222 pesos.
"It was a knee-jerk reaction to the cut. But it's a calculated move of the Central Bank. He (central bank) can afford to sell dollars at 26.235 pesos," said a trader.
The day's average was at 26.232 pesos versus 26.218. Volume fell to $114.50 million from $161.10 million.
The Central Bank had dropped its overnight borrowing rate to 11 percent from 12.50 percent, and its overnight lending rate to 13 percent from 14.50 percent.
The cut was made after the peso-dollar market stabilised late last week. Before that, the Central Bank hiked its overnight rates for two successive days to quell the speculation on the peso.
To stop the peso's fall after the rate cut, the Central Bank sold around $23 million at 26.235 pesos, traders said.
Traders predict the Central Bank won't further ease its overnight rates. "Not yet," said a foreign bank trader, adding that such a move may just spawn more speculation on the peso.
